newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Japanese minister to discuss oil deal in Moscow.
newsitem.headline: Japanese minister to discuss oil deal in Moscow.

text.p: Japan's Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda plans to discuss ways of advancing oil projects and other economic co-operation with Russia during a visit to Moscow later this week, a Russian official said on Monday.
Ikeda, who arrives on Thursday for his first visit to Russia since March 1996, is likely to meet President Boris Yeltsin, a Japanese embassy official said.

He will also meet First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov on Friday to discuss trade and economic issues, Nemtsov's spokesman Andrei Pershin said. Nemtsov and Ikeda co-chair a joint Russian-Japan commission on trade and economic issues.
"They will discuss major joint projects including Sakhalin I and Sakhalin II in which Japanese companies are supposed to be taking part," Pershin said. "We want to unblock the way to the agreement."
The two projects are production-sharing oil and gas deals with Western and Japanese companies in the Far Eastern Russian island of Sakhalin near Japan.
Pershin said the Russian government was working on documents to improve conditions for the projects.
Nemtsov also plans to visit Japan for the second meeting of the commission in mid June, Pershin said.
The foreign ministry declined to give details of Ikeda's programme.

Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodionov finished a visit to Japan on Sunday, during which he promised expanded defence exchanges with Tokyo and gave Moscow's blessing to closer military ties between Japan and the United States.
Relations between Japan and Russia have been strained by a dispute over a group of islands which Moscow seized in the closing stages of World War Two and calls the Kurile Islands.
Japan demands the return of the islands, which it calls the Northern Territories. Because of the dispute, the two countries have never signed a World War Two peace treaty.
